Step 1: Daphnia/Schistosoma sampling Set Eppendorf ThermoMixer with agitation to 37°C. 1. Cut a 1 mL pipette tip to create larger opening 2. Catch a single daphnia with pipette 3. Take a microphotograph 4. Remove all water by pipetting with 100 μL tip; or Perfuse S.mansoni worms and take single worm as dry as possible with forceps 5. Wash once with 50 μL of cold 1x PBS buffer and remove all supernatant by pipetting, being careful not to remove your sample; 6. Add to each sample 25 μl 2× TD buffer 2.5 μl TDE1 0.5 μl 1% IGEPAL 22 μl Nuclease-free water This gives 50 μL of transposase mixture for each sample. Pipette up and down 10 times to disrupt cells. Proceed immediately to step 2.

Step 2: Chromatin Tagmentation This step uses the Nextera Tn5 transposome to tagment the chromatin, which is a process that fragments the chromatin and tags the DNA with adapter sequences in a single step. 1. Tagmentation reactions is incubated at 37°C for 30 min in an Eppendorf ThermoMixer with agitation at 300 rpm. 2. Tagmented chromatin is immediately purified using a QIAGEN MinElute Reaction Cleanup kit (#28204) or a QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (#28106), and purified DNA is eluted into 20 μl of elution buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8)

Run the remaining 45 μl PCR reaction with the additional number of cycles and purify with a QIAGEN MinElute Reaction Cleanup kit (#28204) or a QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (#28106) or similar, and elute with 20 μl of elution buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8). Run it on a 1.5% agarose gel or a Bioanalyzer chip. You should see a ladder that corresponds to the nucleosomefree region and multiple nucleosome-size fragments (one nucleosome = about 150 bp). A single band at around 150bp indicates sample degradation or over-fragmentation. Ideally, five bands should be obtained, three bands are acceptable (figure 2). Fig. 2. Bottom lane: too strong fragmentation, thus Tn5 incubation time needs to be decreased.

steps.title: Double-sided AMPure XP purification
steps.instruction: Enrich nucleosome‑free fragments (~300 bp) and remove primer dimers using two‑step AMPure XP bead clean‑up.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 45 µL of the library to an Eppendorf tube (or directly use a PCR tube).
Add 22.5 µL AMPure XP beads (0.5× the original volume) to remove large fragments; pipet up and down 10 times to mix thoroughly.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Place the tube in a magnetic rack for 5 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Add 58.5 µL AMPure XP beads (1.3× the original volume) to remove small fragments; pipet up and down 10 times to mix thoroughly.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Place the tube in a magnetic rack for 5 minutes.
Wash the beads with 200 µL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol; pipet ethanol over the beads 10 times, then discard the ethanol and ensure all ethanol is removed.
Leave the tube on the magnetic rack with the cap open for 3 to 10 minutes (depending on ambient humidity) until beads appear ‘glowing’ but not wet; avoid over‑drying.
Resuspend the beads in 20 µL nuclease‑free water; pipet up and down 10 times to mix thoroughly.
Place the tube back on the magnetic rack for 1‑5 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant (purified library) to a new tube.
Optional: perform size selection with a Diagenode IP‑Star instrument targeting 320 bp fragments.

steps.title: Library size profiling and quantification
steps.instruction: Assess fragment size distribution and concentration before sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Run the purified library on an Agilent Bioanalyzer using the High Sensitivity DNA Assay to obtain size profiles (expected 150‑800 bp).
Quantify the library using either the Bioanalyzer data or a KAPA library quantification kit.
Proceed to sequencing with the quantified library.

description: Notes It would certainly be good to have always the same number of fragments after Tn5 incubation. It could be envisaged to incubate aliquots of each sample for 10, 20 and 30 min, and then use the sample from the incubation time that provides a fixed, e.g. 3-nucleosome peaks for all samples.
